tiers.name: Part I: Key News & Developments
tiers.description: Macro economy, politics, social security, international relations, industry and key client movements in Paraguay

tiers.name: Part II: Analysis & Recommendations
tiers.description: Enterprise impact assessment and China-specific strategic recommendations

events.title: BCP holds policy rate at 5.50% as inflation stays at 1.7% and the 2026 growth forecast is raised to 5.0% (2026-10-23)
events.summary: The Central Bank's Monetary Policy Committee voted unanimously on 23 October to keep the policy rate at 5.50%, citing annual inflation of 1.7% in September (core 1.5%, monthly 0.1%) and activity growth of 6.7% year-on-year in August as measured by the IMAEP. The BCP raised its 2026 GDP growth projection from 4.5% to 5.0% and cut its end-2026 inflation forecast from 3.3% to 3.0%, with the core forecast lowered from 2.8% to 2.2%. Expectations remain anchored at 3.5%, the centre of the target range. The committee flagged external risks from Middle East geopolitical tensions, high oil prices and the prospect of higher US rates. The next policy meeting is scheduled for 20 November.

events.title: October BCP survey keeps 2026 inflation at 3.0% and cuts the end-year exchange-rate forecast to G. 5,905/USD (2026-10-19)
events.summary: The BCP's October Survey of Economic Variables Expectations, collected to 9 October, keeps median end-2026 inflation at 3.0% and the 2027 and twelve-month horizons at 3.5%. Respondents expect monthly inflation of 0.2% in October and 0.3% in November, GDP growth of 4.5% in 2026 and 4.0% in 2027, and a policy rate of 5.50% through end-2026 before easing to 5.25% at end-2027. The exchange-rate median was cut sharply to G. 5,815 for October, G. 5,850 for November, G. 5,905 at end-2026 and G. 6,185 at end-2027, from G. 6,100 for end-2026 in the September survey, reflecting the guaraní's continued appreciation.

events.title: Fiscal deficit reaches 2.0% of GDP through September, 3.0% annualised, as revenues grow only 1.6% (2026-10-20)
events.summary: The September public-finance report puts the January-September central-government deficit at G. 7.82 trillion (USD 1,257.8 million), equal to 2.0% of GDP versus 0.9% in the same period of 2025. On an annualised basis the gap reaches about 3.0% of GDP, close to USD 2.0 billion, and the MEF projects 3.2% for the full year against an original 1.5% target. Revenue rose only 1.6% while trade-related taxes fell 11% and Itaipú royalties and compensation dropped 25.9%, both hit by the guaraní's 11.9% appreciation through September. Wages, pensions and debt service absorb close to 70% of public financing, and the Caja Fiscal pension scheme shows a deficit above 43% of its annual budget.

events.title: Guaraní closes the week near G. 5,776/USD after touching a multi-year low, squeezing exporters and fiscal revenue (2026-10-23)
events.summary: The BCP's weighted-average reference rate was G. 5,764.73 per dollar on 23 October, with the 13:00 quote at G. 5,776.68, after G. 5,801.08 on 22 October and a multi-year low of about G. 5,694 on 13 October. The guaraní has appreciated 11.9% year-to-date through September, one of the strongest performances in the region, and the central bank has not intervened in the spot market. Exporters warn that margins are being compressed and that dollar revenues converted into guaraníes no longer cover local costs, while the Treasury loses guaraní revenue from trade taxes and Itaipú royalties. The October survey still sees G. 5,905 at end-2026, implying only a modest correction from current levels.

events.title: September exports rise 25.4% to USD 1,834M but the monthly trade deficit widens to USD 118.2M; January-September surplus reaches USD 712M (2026-10-20)
events.summary: Paraguay exported USD 1,834.1 million in September, up 25.4% year-on-year, with primary products up 20.9%, agro-industrial manufactures up 23.4% and industrial manufactures up 41.6%. Imports reached USD 1,952.2 million, up 23.5%, driven by consumption goods (+20.9%), intermediate goods (+41.4%) and capital goods (+11.7%), leaving a monthly deficit of USD 118.16 million, slightly above the USD 117.73 million gap a year earlier. For January-September, exports totalled USD 15,972.6 million (+25.7%) and imports USD 15,260.6 million (+15%), producing a cumulative surplus of USD 712 million compared with a USD 555.5 million deficit in 2025. Soy and its derivatives account for 41% of exports and rose 45.1% to USD 3,107.2 million.

events.title: MEF presents a G. 166.3 trillion 2027 budget to the bicameral committee, with a 3.9% deficit and USD 2.1 billion of new debt (2026-10-22)
events.summary: Economy Minister Óscar Lovera presented the 2027 budget priorities to the bicameral budget committee on 22 October. The draft totals G. 166.32 trillion (about USD 25.75 billion), 11.2% above the 2026 approved budget, and projects a 3.9% of GDP deficit under an exceptional escape from the 1.5% fiscal-responsibility limit. New borrowing is about USD 2.1 billion, with total financing needs including refinancing near USD 2.8 billion. Health receives 62% of the spending increase (over USD 1.2 billion, 78% of it to clear accumulated arrears), pensions rise 20%, and an addendum includes a 5% teacher pay increase worth USD 47 million. The bill remained in committee with no floor vote in either chamber.

events.title: Peña defends BCP independence and promises to work with opposition mayors during his final 22 months (2026-10-20)
events.summary: At the Council of Ministers on 20 October, President Santiago Peña defended the Central Bank's autonomy amid congressional pressure over monetary and exchange-rate policy, and pledged not to sideline opposition mayors in the remaining 22 months of his term. He set a goal of advancing "with a firm step" on investment and public management, while acknowledging tensions within the ruling Colorado Party over the 2027 budget and the 2028 succession. The statement is significant for investors because it signals continuity at the BCP and a willingness to keep mayors of other parties inside the public-investment pipeline ahead of the municipal and general electoral cycle.

events.title: Peña outlines solar and small modular nuclear plans, positioning energy as the anchor of the next investment cycle (2026-10-22)
events.summary: President Peña said his government will develop solar generation and small modular reactors to guarantee long-term electricity supply, and confirmed that a US company is exploring uranium deposits. The plan is presented as complementary to Itaipú hydropower and aimed at data-centre and industrial demand, following the Crusoe-Araico announcement and the Yguazú Digital project. The ANDE has already signed a 15-year supply contract of up to 286 MW for a data centre. Critics, including the ANDE workers' union and Brazilian politicians, warn that preferential tariffs and large-scale consumption could accelerate an energy deficit toward 2030 and that the agreements lack public disclosure.

events.title: Deputies fast-track a bill imposing up to 90 years in prison; a separate financial-panic bill advances amid censorship concerns (2026-10-23)
events.summary: The Chamber of Deputies granted a 15-day priority motion to a bill by Deputy Rubén Rubín that would impose sentences of up to 90 years, with review after 50 years served, for aggravated homicide including femicide, parricide, contract killing and terrorism, as well as sexual crimes, aggravated robbery and certain frauds. Separately, ruling-party Deputy Alejandro Aguilera presented a bill punishing with up to 10 years anyone who deliberately spreads false information capable of triggering bank runs; the opposition called it censorship. The Senate legislation committee also recommended raising penalties for organised cattle rustling to 15 years and expanding the age range in sexual-crime articles. None of the bills is law yet.

events.title: PCC-linked commando kills a woman and abducts a man in Pedro Juan Caballero; the body is found later (2026-10-19)
events.summary: About ten armed men stormed a home in Barrio Obrero, Pedro Juan Caballero, on Monday 19 October, killing Carolina Benítez Arce, 27, and abducting Marcelo Ruan Ortiz Lázaro, 26, whose body was later found on a rural road. Prosecutors and the homicide department raided an apartment complex in Virgen de Caacupé and seized the building's DVR, which showed a white Toyota Fortuner leaving with the hit squad. A suspect, Eder Eligio Gómez Torres, was identified and remains at large. Investigators link the attack to a dispute between drug-trafficking groups with ties to the First Capital Command (PCC), underlining the persistence of organised-crime violence on the Brazilian border.

events.title: Three raids in Minga Guazú over an assault on a Brazilian family; two suspects arrested (2026-10-20)
events.summary: Police raided three properties in Minga Guazú, Alto Paraná, on 20 October in connection with an armed assault on a Brazilian family and a second robbery, arresting two alleged gang members. Officers seized ammunition, tactical clothing, mobile phones, a DVR, a Fiat Strada pickup, a drone, vehicle plates and registration documents. The operation is part of a broader push against armed robbery networks operating in the tri-border area, where criminal groups exploit the same logistics corridors used by legitimate trade. The case adds to a run of violent incidents in Alto Paraná that has prompted calls for a stronger police and military presence in the department.

events.title: SENAD Operation IGNIS arrests an alleged close operative of "Macho" in Canindeyú (2026-10-22)
events.summary: On 22 October the anti-drug secretariat SENAD, supported by the CODI special forces, the FTC, SAP 5 and BIMI, detained José Ignacio Hermoza Ledesma, known as "Nacho", on a rural property in Colonia Americana, Corpus Christi department of Canindeyú. He is accused of being a close collaborator of Felipe Santiago Acosta Riveros, alias "Macho", one of the country's most wanted alleged traffickers. Two mobile phones were seized. The operation follows a series of raids against the "Macho" network and signals continuing pressure on cannabis and cocaine routes in the northern border departments, a region where illegal armed groups and cattle rustling overlap.

events.title: Paraná floods displace 1,988 families and affect 4,253 across four departments (2026-10-21)
events.summary: The National Emergency Secretariat reported on 20-21 October that 4,253 families had been affected by the Paraná river flood in Itapúa, Misiones, Alto Paraná and Ñeembucú. Of these, 1,988 families had been evacuated, 1,369 were receiving assistance and 2,672 were still waiting for help; Alto Paraná was the hardest-hit department, followed by Ñeembucú. In Ayolas the river stood near 6.40 metres with 3,438 people in 14 shelters. Itaipú and Yacyretá opened spillways, 14 migration posts were temporarily closed, and forecasts of up to 150 millimetres of additional rain threatened to worsen conditions over the weekend. The flood is disrupting road access and port operations in the south and east.

events.title: SENAD raids an Asunción barbershop-tattoo studio used as a cocaine front; 199 grams seized (2026-10-23)
events.summary: On 23 October SENAD agents raided a barbershop and tattoo studio in Barrio Obrero, Asunción, that was allegedly used as a front for retail cocaine sales. Officers seized 199 grams of cocaine, cash and other evidence and detained one person. The case is part of a push against micro-trafficking points in the capital's central neighbourhoods, which have multiplied as larger trafficking networks fragment into retail distribution. For companies operating in Asunción, the raid is a reminder that petty crime and drug retailing remain concentrated in specific central and peri-central neighbourhoods.

events.title: US opens an INL anti-narcotics office in Asunción, its first Southern Cone regional hub, with a USD 11.75 million package (2026-10-21)
events.summary: At the end of Under Secretary Christopher Landau's visit on 19-21 October, Washington announced the creation of the first INL (Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs) office in Asunción, which will also coordinate INL programmes across the Southern Cone. The package totals USD 11.75 million: USD 6.25 million against transnational organised crime and USD 5.5 million against terrorist financing and narco-terrorism, including a new counter-terrorism centre. The two governments signed an air-interdiction assistance agreement and a memorandum to implement the PISCES migration and border-control system. A regional counter-terrorism adviser will be posted to Asunción for the first time. The moves sit under Washington's "Shield of the Americas" framework.

events.title: Paraguay becomes the 26th signatory of the US-led Pax Silica AI supply-chain coalition (2026-10-23)
events.summary: President Peña announced on 23 October that Paraguay had joined Pax Silica, the US-led coalition on artificial-intelligence supply chains, becoming its 26th signatory. Foreign Minister Rubén Ramírez Lezcano and US Under Secretary for Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg signed the declaration at the State Department. Peña framed the move as part of a shift "from being technology consumers to technology producers", leveraging Paraguay's hydropower and critical minerals. The accession complements the data-centre and semiconductor-supply discussions held during his Washington visit and deepens Paraguay's alignment with US technology policy, a stance that carries explicit risk in its relations with China.

events.title: Peña pledges critical-minerals supply cooperation with US Treasury Secretary Bessent (2026-10-22)
events.summary: During his 21-23 October visit to Washington, President Peña met Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and committed Paraguay to strengthening critical-minerals supply chains for the United States. He also spoke at George Washington University and at the Inter-American Dialogue at the OAS. US officials confirmed a USD 12 million investment by Uranium Energy Corp in Paraguay and discussed the exploration of uranium and rare-earth elements. The visit included a reported private meeting with CIA Director John Ratcliffe on the anti-drug office to be installed in Asunción. The minerals agenda is the commercial counterpart to the security and AI-supply-chain agreements announced the same week.

events.title: Brazil questions Paraguay's use of Itaipú for data centres; ANDE chief says Asunción need not consult Brasília (2026-10-23)
events.summary: After ANDE signed a 15-year supply contract of up to 286 MW with Kuntur (Araico) for a data centre, Brazilian media and politicians argued that Paraguay was diverting Itaipú surplus away from the Brazilian market, with some claiming the country had "sold half of Itaipú". ANDE president Miguel Báez rejected the criticism, saying Paraguay does not need Brazil's authorisation to use its own 50% share of the binational plant. Itaipú clarified that each margin may receive foreign authorities and that the treaty guarantees each country half of the energy. President Peña said there had been no progress on the Annex C tariff review; the provisional tariff remains USD 19.28 per kW-month for 2024-2026, while Paraguay seeks a three-to-five-year medium-term tariff from 2027.

events.title: Taiwan-Paraguay Polytechnic University advances in Luque with USD 20 million in non-reimbursable cooperation; opening set for July 2027 (2026-10-24)
events.summary: Construction of the Taiwan-Paraguay Polytechnic University in Luque is advancing: 20,000 square metres, about 40 classrooms and 13 laboratories, financed with roughly USD 20 million of non-reimbursable Taiwanese cooperation. The project was agreed in 2018 with National Taiwan University of Science and Technology and is due to open in July 2027. It currently trains about 300 students, and more than 800 Paraguayans have received scholarships in Taiwan. The campus is part of the technological cooperation package that includes Yguazú Digital and the Taiwan-Paraguay industrial park, and it comes as Asunción reaffirms its diplomatic recognition of Taipei after China's 12 October sanctions on MITIC minister Gustavo Villate.

sections.title: V. Industry Focus: Telecom, Digital Energy & AI

events.title: Crusoe and Araico announce Latin America's first Crusoe AI data centre in Paraguay, powered by Itaipú and scalable to 280 MW (2026-10-22)
events.summary: US firm Crusoe Energy and Paraguayan group Araico announced on 22 October the construction of Crusoe's first Latin American data centre, powered by Itaipú energy and connected to the ANDE grid. The first phase is estimated at USD 300 million for 6 MW and about 2,000 Nvidia Blackwell AI processors, with construction starting in March 2027 and initial operation in mid-2027. Capacity is designed to scale to 106 MW of technology infrastructure and up to 280 MW in the long term, within the "Iguazú AI City" campus in Colonia Yguazú, Alto Paraná, near the Yguazú substation. The project is backed by a power-purchase agreement with ANDE at a reported USD 45-48/MWh at 220 kV with a 2.5% annual adjustment. US officials called it potentially one of the largest private investments in Paraguay's history.

events.title: ANDE signs a 15-year PPA with Kuntur (Araico) for up to 286 MW at USD 48.91-56.39/MWh (2026-10-21)
events.summary: ANDE formalised resolution 52552/2026 approving a 15-year power-purchase contract with Kuntur, an Araico affiliate, for up to 286 MW to supply a data-centre campus, at tariffs of USD 48.91-56.39/MWh. The contract is one of the largest long-term electricity commitments ever signed by the state utility and is tied to the Crusoe-Araico project. The ANDE workers' union Sitrande questioned the preferential treatment and warned about the impact on the grid and on energy sovereignty, while Brazilian actors raised concerns about the use of Itaipú surplus. The resolution also raises questions about whether the commitment fits within the legal ceiling for ANDE's long-term contracts and about who bears the cost of network reinforcements.

events.title: Peña meets Anthropic's Teresa Carlson and presents the Yguazú Digital 10 MW to 1 GW AI campus (2026-10-23)
events.summary: On 23 October President Peña met Teresa Carlson, Anthropic's global head of public sector, to explore cooperation on artificial intelligence and presented the Yguazú Digital project developed with Taiwan. The campus is planned in three phases of 10 MW, 100 MW and 1,000 MW of operating capacity, combining Paraguayan energy with Taiwanese technology and investment. The meeting took place during Peña's Washington visit, alongside the Pax Silica accession and the critical-minerals talks. MITIC minister Gustavo Villate has said the Taiwan technology projects, including Yguazú Digital, the technology park and the polytechnic university, will continue despite China's 12 October countermeasures against him.

events.title: Deputies request ANDE reports on telecom operators' use of its poles for fibre and aerial cabling (2026-10-22)
events.summary: The Chamber of Deputies approved a request for information to ANDE on the use of its poles by telecom, fibre-optic, cable and internet companies, covering contracts, revenue, maintenance costs and the risks of aerial cabling. The request reflects growing scrutiny of the shared-infrastructure regime as fibre and 5G deployments accelerate and operators seek faster, cheaper ways to reach new areas. For operators, the outcome could affect pole-access fees and deployment timelines; for ANDE, it is an opportunity to formalise a revenue stream that has been largely informal. The information request does not change the rules yet but signals that Congress intends to legislate on passive infrastructure.

events.title: Conatel extends the public consultation on the 2026-2030 National Telecom Plan, targeting 30% 5G coverage and USD 2.31 billion in capex (2026-10-22)
events.summary: Conatel extended the public consultation on the draft 2026-2030 National Telecommunications Plan, which is built on three pillars: infrastructure and coverage, quality and regulation, and affordability and digital inclusion. The plan targets 30% population coverage for 5G, 95.6% for 4G and 265 districts connected to a fibre-optic backbone by 2030, with estimated capital expenditure of USD 2.313 billion. The extension gives operators and industry groups more time to comment on spectrum, deployment obligations and passive-infrastructure rules. It follows criticism from the mobile operators' chamber over the design of the eight sub-bands in the 3.5 GHz band and the exclusion of Chinese equipment from the 5G tender.

events.title: Nubicom activates 34 5G sites but relies on Ufinet fibre and Copaco/Vox sites; only two subscribers (2026-10-23)
events.summary: Nubicom has activated 34 5G radio bases, above the 20-22 required for its first year: 28 in Asunción, two in Lambaré, two in Fernando de la Mora and two in Luque. Thirty-three sites use Nokia equipment and one uses Tejas Networks, a Rakuten subsidiary, pointing to a possible Open RAN architecture. The company leases 100 Gbps backbone links from Ufinet and uses Copaco/Vox sites, so most of its transport and real estate is third-party. Nubicom has declared USD 24 million for its core and 157 radio bases, of which USD 13.5 million corresponds to the 34 inspected sites and the core. It holds 200 MHz in 3.5 GHz but has only two active subscribers, probably fixed-wireless access, and is not obliged to offer mobile telephony during its first five years.

events.title: Comptroller questions Nubicom's commercial operation; Conatel says the licence could be revoked if service is not proven (2026-10-21)
events.summary: Conatel declared that Nubicom had met its initial 5G deployment obligation, but admitted that coverage is limited and that the company had only two subscribers. The Comptroller General's Office questioned whether commercial service is effectively being provided and warned that the licence could be revoked if Nubicom fails to demonstrate it. Senator Rafael Filizzola alleged corruption in the award and said Paraguay could lose close to USD 200 million in expected investment. Conatel defended its autonomy and said it is monitoring the case. The dispute matters for the market because Nubicom is one of four 5G licence holders and its failure would leave a large block of 3.5 GHz spectrum underused.

events.title: Personal offers 15 days of free calls and internet in flood shelters in Ayolas and Ciudad del Este (2026-10-21)
events.summary: Personal, operated by Núcleo S.A., enabled 15 days of free calls and provided internet connectivity in shelters in Ayolas and Ciudad del Este for families affected by the Paraná river and Acaraymí stream floods. The measure covers both its mobile and fixed networks and is part of the operator's emergency-response protocol. Beyond the social dimension, the episode tests network resilience in the south and east, where flooding has disrupted roads and power. Personal is also the operator that must present its detailed 5G engineering plan within 90 days of its August licence and activate its first 5G radio base by February 2027.

events.title: Claro leads Paraguay's 5G coverage with 23.75% nationally and 77.7% in Asunción (latest available data, October 2026)
events.summary: The nPerf barometer places Claro first in both 4G and 5G coverage in Paraguay, with 86.67% national 4G coverage, 23.75% national 5G coverage and 77.7% 5G coverage in Asunción. Claro launched the country's first commercial 5G network in December 2025 with a USD 35 million investment and Nokia equipment, and has extended coverage to 12 cities including Gran Asunción, Ciudad del Este, Encarnación, Coronel Oviedo, Pedro Juan Caballero, Villarrica, Hernandarias and Cambyretá. The company says it has exceeded its licence obligations in the central area. The main constraint on mass adoption is now the installed base of 5G-compatible devices rather than network coverage.

sections.title: VII. Integrated Impact Analysis for Business Operations
sections.impact_analysis:
🟡 The exchange rate is now the binding constraint, not inflation. The guaraní closed the week at G. 5,764.73-5,776.68 per dollar (BCP, 23 October), after touching about G. 5,694 on 13 October, and has appreciated 11.9% year-to-date through September. The BCP held the policy rate at 5.50% on 23 October with inflation at 1.7% and core at 1.5%, and its October survey cut the end-2026 rate forecast to G. 5,905 from G. 6,100 a month earlier. For any operation with dollar revenue and guaraní costs, margins compress mechanically every month; for the Treasury, the same appreciation cut trade taxes by 11% and Itaipú royalties by 25.9% through September. Hedging is no longer optional, and contracts priced at G. 6,300-6,600 in 2025 are already loss-making on conversion.

🟡 The fiscal deterioration is structural and the 2027 budget does not close it. The January-September deficit reached 2.0% of GDP (G. 7.82 trillion, USD 1,257.8 million), or about 3.0% annualised, against an original 1.5% target; the MEF projects 3.2% for 2026 and the 2027 draft assumes 3.9% under an exceptional escape from the fiscal rule. Revenue grew only 1.6%, wages, pensions and debt service absorb close to 70% of financing, and the Caja Fiscal deficit exceeds 43% of its annual budget. The 2027 budget adds USD 2.1 billion of new debt and a 5% teacher raise worth USD 47 million. Suppliers to the public sector should expect slower payment cycles and more pressure to accept Treasury paper or renegotiated terms.

🟡 The data-centre and energy boom is real but carries regulatory and political risk. Crusoe and Araico announced a USD 300 million first phase (6 MW, about 2,000 Nvidia Blackwell processors, operating from mid-2027) scalable to 280 MW, backed by an ANDE 15-year contract of up to 286 MW at USD 48.91-56.39/MWh. The project is one of the largest private investments in Paraguay's history, but the ANDE union, Brazilian politicians and the Comptroller have all raised questions about preferential tariffs, grid capacity and the use of Itaipú surplus. The Annex C tariff review remains unresolved, with the provisional USD 19.28/kW-month rate extended for 2024-2026 and Paraguay seeking a three-to-five-year medium-term tariff from 2027. Any energy-intensive project should model a tariff renegotiation scenario and secure firm transmission capacity.

🟡 Security and climate risks are concentrated in Alto Paraná and the south. The PCC-linked attack in Pedro Juan Caballero on 19 October, the Minga Guazú raids on 20 October and the SENAD operations in Canindeyú and Asunción show that organised crime remains active along the Brazilian border and in the capital's retail drug trade. The Paraná flood affected 4,253 families in four departments, displaced 1,988 and closed 14 migration posts, disrupting roads and port access. The US INL office and the USD 11.75 million security package announced on 21 October may improve coordination over time but will not change the operating picture in the next two quarters.

🟢 Telecom offers the clearest near-term commercial opportunity. Claro leads 5G coverage at 23.75% nationally and 77.7% in Asunción; Tigo and Personal must activate their first 5G radio bases by February 2027 and plan 250-500 sites and about USD 79 million of joint investment; Nubicom has 34 sites but only two subscribers and is under Comptroller scrutiny; the 2026-2030 National Telecom Plan targets 30% 5G coverage and USD 2.313 billion of capex. The 3.5 GHz sub-band auction and the exclusion of Chinese equipment remain the main structural barriers for Chinese vendors, while passive-infrastructure rules (ANDE poles) and the PNT consultation are the near-term policy levers.

sections.title: VIII. Targeted Recommendations for Chinese Enterprises
sections.impact_analysis:
🔴 Protect revenue before anything else. With the guaraní at G. 5,764-5,777 and the BCP forecasting only G. 5,905 by December, dollar-revenue operations should lock in forward contracts now, re-price or re-denominate 2025-vintage contracts signed at G. 6,300-6,600, and add exchange-rate clauses to new EPC, service and supply agreements. The BCP's forward window has grown as local exporters reach the same conclusion; the cost of hedging is far below the cost of realising another 5-10% appreciation. For guaraní-revenue operations, the same move protects margins against a rebound if US rates stay higher for longer.

🟡 Treat public-sector exposure as credit risk. The January-September deficit is 2.0% of GDP (3.0% annualised), the 2027 budget assumes 3.9%, and the MEF projects 3.2% for 2026 against a 1.5% rule. Payment delays, Treasury paper and renegotiation requests are likely. Prioritise private clients, require guarantees or escrow for public contracts, and stress-test receivables against a 90-180 day delay. The 2027 budget's health allocation (62% of the increase, 78% to arrears) may unlock some health-sector payments, but the overall fiscal squeeze is not easing.

🟡 Engage the energy and data-centre pipeline early, with political-risk pricing. The Crusoe-Araico project (USD 300 million first phase, 280 MW long-term) and the ANDE 15-year PPA at USD 48.91-56.39/MWh create procurement demand for substations, cooling, fibre, backup power and construction services. But the ANDE union, Brazilian politicians and the Comptroller are contesting preferential tariffs and Itaipú use, and the Annex C review is unresolved. Bid only with firm transmission capacity, clear curtailment rules and a tariff-renegotiation scenario; avoid contracts that assume the current preferential rate survives to 2030.

🔴 Manage the Taiwan-China fault line explicitly. China sanctioned MITIC minister Gustavo Villate on 12 October over his Taiwan ties, and Paraguay responded by reaffirming its recognition of Taipei and joining the US-led Pax Silica coalition on 23 October. Chinese enterprises should avoid any commercial or personal exposure to sanctioned individuals and should not assume that Paraguay's Taiwan relationship will change in the near term. The exclusion of Chinese equipment from the 5G tender is a structural barrier; focus on non-RAN segments (fibre, power, data-centre fit-out, enterprise IT) where the restriction does not bind, and keep a clear compliance file for US secondary-sanctions exposure.

🟢 Prioritise the telecom rollout and digital-infrastructure supply chain. Tigo and Personal must activate their first 5G sites by February 2027 and plan 250-500 sites and about USD 79 million; Claro is expanding from 12 cities; Nubicom has 157 radio bases to deploy but only two subscribers and regulatory risk. The PNT 2026-2030 targets 265 districts with fibre backbone, 95.6% 4G and 30% 5G coverage, with USD 2.313 billion of capex. The ANDE pole-access review and the PNT consultation are the immediate policy windows; position for passive infrastructure, fibre, power and O&M work rather than spectrum-dependent RAN.

🟡 Build security and climate contingency into delivery schedules. Alto Paraná (Pedro Juan Caballero, Minga Guazú) and the southern flood corridor are the main operational risks; the Paraná flood displaced 1,988 families and closed 14 migration posts. Site security, convoy rules, insurance and alternate logistics routes should be standard for projects in those areas, and delivery schedules should carry weather and road-access buffers for the November-April rainy season.
